Growth & demand: While these disruptions did constrain our ability to fully service demand and resulted in some loss of production opportunities of about 10% of volume during the quarter, the business still delivered record volumes and financial performance.

On revenue, volumes reached an all-time high of over 1.4 million Bajaj Auto Limited July 21, 2026 units, a growth of 29% year -on-year, while revenue from operations crossed the INR17,000 crores mark for the very first time, coming in at INR17,244 crores, representing a robust 37% year-on-year growth.

While revenues grew 37%, EBITDA grew by 45% and the ability of the business to convert strong top line growth into higher earnings despite operating in an extremely volatile and challenging environment.
Margins & costs: Volumes at 1.4 million, revenue of INR17,000 crores, EBITDA of INR3,500 crores and PAT of INR3,000 crores, along with EBITDA margins of 20.9%.

On commodity inflation, as many of you would recall, when we last met in May, I had indicated that the operating environment had turned sharply inflationary, and we were estimating commodity inflation to be in the range of 3.5% to 4%.
EBITDA margins inched up to 20.9%, an improvement of 10 basis points sequentially despite the hyperinflationary commodity environment that I'd spoken about.
Capex & expansion: By our estimates, a disproportionate share of this expansion was captured by us, doubling retails year -on-year and delivering a market share of almost 60% in retail terms.
Capacity expansion has been undertaken, with an immediate and medium -term focus to enable us better serve the growing market.

So, with an eye on the future, we are undertaking an expansion of capacity by almost 25% from the current 7 million units per annum across different businesses to progressively go up to 9 million units per annum.
